sources.citation: eKitabu. 2024. Malawian Sign Language Early Grade Reading Materials Adaptation (DTF final narrative report). DOI 10.53832/ekitabu.1023.
sources.note: Nothing. Project report on adapting ten storybooks into MSL video with MANAD; no linguistic description.

sources.citation: MANAD (Malawi National Association of the Deaf). Sign Language programme page and 'Download the MANAD Dictionary App today!' (2024-12-19); Malawian Sign Language Dictionary (MSLD), first edition c. 2020, produced with the Finnish Association of the Deaf.
sources.note: Nothing. Video sign dictionary (app/website); page gives history (first deaf school 1968, Maryview, Chiradzulu; MSL emerged naturally in deaf schools) and documentation project 2017-2020; no grammar or phonology text.

sources.citation: Minton-Ryan, Carol A., Mary Sorola, Jackson Brown & Pamela R. Perez. 2019. A lexicostatistical study: Phonological similarity between American and Malawi Sign Languages. LASU: Journal of the Linguistics Association of SADC Universities 5(5): 87-103.
sources.note: Nothing. It is a 50/100-sign lexicostatistical comparison with ASL on four manual parameters (handshape, location, palm orientation, movement; facial expression omitted), finding 32-39% similarity; states on p. 87 that 'Malawian sign language remains undocumented'. No mention of stress, prosody, accent or prominence anywhere (a full-text search for stress/accent full text).

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2017. Change Request Number 2017-011: create [lws] Malawian Sign Language (submitted by Jackson Brown, Mary Sorola, Carol Minton; adopted 2018-01-23). SIL International.
sources.note: Nothing. Administrative form: a California Baptist University team documented 400+ signs at Embangweni School for the Deaf (2015-2016); asserts MSL 'has all the markers of a complete sign language in terms of phonology, morphology, syntax, and semantics' and its own syntax influenced by Chichewa/Chitumbuka, with no ASL relationship; no linguistic description; 'Knowledge from published sources' left blank.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2016/2017. Request for New Language Code Element in ISO 639-3: Malawian Sign Language [lws] (Mary Sorola, Jackson Brown), companion to CR 2017-011.
sources.note: Nothing. Autonym 'Malawi Sign'; used in Mzimba, Karonga, Zomba, Lilongwe, Dedza, Embangweni, Blantyre, Mua, Mzuzu; 'Minimal resources are available. This team is working to create a dictionary and eventual corpora'.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 entry mala1549 (Hammarström et al.); Wikidata Q47522462; Wikipedia 'Malawian Sign Language'.
sources.note: Nothing. Glottolog lists only Minton-Ryan et al. 2019 (comparative) and Ethnologue; classifies MSL as a presumed sign-language isolate ('only 32-39% cognates' with ASL). Wikipedia is a stub citing only Ethnologue.
